# The Gamma function

In this notes we will create an interactive app to explore how the parameters of the gamma distribution affect is PDF. Lets start by loading the required packages:

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(krulRutils)
library(latex2exp)
```

We now build the corresponding app:

```{r}
#| label: app

ui <- fluidPage(
    column(
      4,
        tags$h4("Parámetros"),
        sliderInput("alpha", "α (shape)", min = 0.2, max = 20, value = 2, step = 0.1),
        sliderInput("beta",  "β (rate)",  min = 0.05, max = 10, value = 1, step = 0.05),

        tags$hr(),

        tags$h4("Visualización"),
        sliderInput("xmax", "X máximo", min = 5, max = 100, value = 15, step = 1),

        tags$hr(),
    ),
    column(
      8,
      plotOutput("gammaPlot"),
      verbatimTextOutput("summaryText")
    )
  )

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  gamma_tbl <- reactive({
    x <- seq(0, input$xmax, length.out = 1000)
    tibble(
      x = x,
      fx = dgamma(x, shape = input$alpha, rate = input$beta)
    )
  })

  derived <- reactive({
    alpha <- input$alpha
    beta  <- input$beta

    mean <- alpha / beta
    var  <- alpha / (beta^2)
    sd   <- sqrt(var)
    skew <- 2 / sqrt(alpha)
    exk  <- 6 / alpha


    list(mean = mean, var = var, sd = sd, skew = skew, exk = exk)
  })

  output$gammaPlot <- renderPlot({
    tbl <- gamma_tbl()
    d <- derived()

    p <- ggplot(tbl, aes(x = x, y = fx)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      labs(
        title = TeX(paste0("Gamma: \\; \\alpha = ", input$alpha, ",\\; \\beta = ", input$beta,
                           " \\;\\; (\\text{rate})")),
        x = TeX("$x$"),
        y = TeX("$f(x)$")
      )

    p + theme_krul()
  })

  output$summaryText <- renderText({
    d <- derived()
    paste0(
      "Resumen (con β como rate)\n",
      "Media = α/β = ", signif(d$mean, 6), "\n",
      "Varianza = α/β^2 = ", signif(d$var, 6), "    (SD = ", signif(d$sd, 6), ")\n",
      "Asimetría = 2/sqrt(α) = ", signif(d$skew, 6), "\n",
      "Curtosis excesiva = 6/α = ", signif(d$exk, 6), "\n"
    )
  })
}
```

Notice how as $\alpha$ increases, the distribution becomes more and more symmetric.

```{r}
#| panel: fill
shinyApp(ui, server)
```
